The '''2014–15 [[Cypriot First Division]]''' was the 76th season of the Cypriot top-level [[Association football|football]] league. It began on 23 August 2014<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/18180|script-title=el:Στις 23 Αυγούστου η πρεμιέρα του νέου Πρωταθλήματος|language=el|publisher=CFA|date=9 April 2014|access-date=9 April 2014}}</ref> and ended on 24 May 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/22546|script-title=el:Πρόγραμμα τελευταίας αγωνιστικής|language=el|publisher=CFA|date=18 May 2015|access-date=18 May 2015}}</ref> [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] were the defending champions.

The league this edition was reduced from 14 to 12 teams: ten teams from the [[2013–14 Cypriot First Division|2013–14 season]] and two promoted teams from the [[2013–14 Cypriot Second Division|2013–14 B1 Division]]. [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] won the league for a 24th successive time and a third consecutive season, after 62 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=cyp/news/newsid=2251216.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150527185446/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=cyp/news/newsid=2251216.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 May 2015|title=APOEL secure league to wrap up Cypriot double|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=24 May 2015|access-date=24 May 2015}}</ref>

==Teams==

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
[[Enosis Neon Paralimni FC|Enosis Neon Paralimni]] and [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were relegated at the end of the first stage of the [[2013–14 Cypriot First Division|2013–14 season]] after finishing in the bottom two places of the table. They were joined by [[Aris Limassol F.C.|Aris Limassol]] and [[AEK Kouklia F.C.|AEK Kouklia]], who finished at the bottom of the second-phase relegation group.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2013–14 Cypriot Second Division|2013–14 B1 Division]] champions [[Ayia Napa F.C.|Ayia Napa]] and runners-up [[Othellos Athienou F.C.|Othellos Athienou]].
